title: Function invoke lattice and graceful choice fallback
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Customers integrating OpenAI-style function/tool calling see intermittent failures and unexpected 'tool_choice' semantics when streaming fragments arrive out-of-order or partial. This PR introduces a canonical invocation envelope (the 'lattice') that sits inside the OpenAI compatibility layer and normalizes incoming tool/function messages into a compact, ordered, idempotent structure. The lattice addresses three customer pain points: 1) streaming fragment reassembly and fragmentation-related field duplication, 2) deterministic tool_choice tie-breaking when multiple candidates are emitted across fragments, and 3) a graceful fallback/backoff policy for tool invocations when downstream tool adapters are busy or transiently failing.

What this PR does (high level): implements a canonical envelope serializer/deserializer in the compat shim; adds a tool schema mapping layer that normalizes names/params across our internal tool registry and OpenAI schemas; introduces a choice arbitration component that accumulates candidate tool choices across fragments and resolves them with configurable tie-breakers (confidence, recency, explicit client preference) rather than first-seen wins; implements a short exponential backoff for automatic noop/fallback to non-tool output when adapters fail or become overloaded; and exposes telemetry for choice provenance and fallback triggers.

Design notes: the lattice is intentionally lightweight: it keeps per-invocation provenance tokens, fragment sequence indices, and a small canonical choice list (choice_id, source_fragment, score_normalized, mapped_schema_ref). Mapping is pluggable: we include a default mapper that handles common OpenAI -> Redwood name and parameter patterns (e.g., openai 'name' vs internal 'tool_id', primitive param coercions). The choice resolver allows ordered tie-breakers configured via API flags (default: score -> explicit preference -> recency).

Migration and compatibility: the compat shim will honour clients that send single-message invocations as before; the lattice only activates for streaming/fragmented payloads or when the incoming message contains more than one candidate. We add a runtime flag to opt-out in case a customer needs legacy behaviour for short windows.

Testing: included unit tests for mapping edge cases (null params, aliased keys), integration tests that simulate fragmented streams with out-of-order delivery, and a small load test for backoff behaviour to ensure we don't excessively fall back under transient adapter saturation. See tests/compat_invoke_lattice_test.py for scenarios. CI initially flagged a flaky integration test; I adjusted the test harness timing and re-ran.

Observability and metrics: new metrics (compat.choice_resolutions, compat.fallbacks, compat.fragment_coalesces) and structured traces that include the canonical choice list and the chosen resolution cause. These are available in the console under the OpenAI-compat dashboard.

Risk and rollout plan: opt-in flag for first 48 hours for a small set of customers, then default-on after telemetry shows stable resolution rates and no increase in error budgets. No breaking API changes expected; documented fallback semantics in the changelog.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Can you clarify how we handle conflicting parameter types across fragments? It looked like we coerce to the first-seen type — why not prefer numeric when ambiguity?

Priya Nair (reply): We coerce using a small heuristic (`number` > `string` > `object`) because numeric coercions are safer for downstream adapters; added tests to cover ambiguous cases and a config flag if customers prefer strict typing.
Jordan Kim: Integration test 03 was flaky on ci/integration_openai_compat. Is there a timing dependency?
Priya Nair (reply): Good catch — the test assumed synchronous adapter ack; updated harness to allow async ack and added a retry window; CI rerun passed.
Ava Martinez: We should expose the resolved choice provenance in traces to help customers debug. Can you add a stable key?
Priya Nair (reply): Added compat.choice_provenance tag to the trace payload and documented it in the dashboard notes.

release_notes: OpenAI-compat: introduce canonical invoke lattice to stabilize fragmented tool/function streaming
Tool mapping: default OpenAI->internal name/param mappings; pluggable mappers for custom registries
Choice arbitration: deterministic tie-breakers and telemetry for provenance
Fallback policy: short exponential backoff with metrics to avoid noisy failures
